title: EEG and motion capture data set for a full-body/joystick rotation task
description: A mobile brain/body imaging (MoBI) dataset combining 157-channel EEG and full-body motion capture from 20 healthy adults performing a spatial heading-change task. Participants followed a moving sphere and returned to their initial heading either by physically rotating on the spot or by using a joystick with a 2D desktop display. The dataset supports investigation of human cortical dynamics during full-body rotation and is formatted according to BIDS.
methods_description: EEG was recorded from 157 active electrodes (129 scalp, 28 neck) at 1000 Hz with a BrainAmp Move system. Motion capture used a PhaseSpace Impulse X2 system with 19 LEDs at 90 Hz. Participants completed a spot-rotation task in a virtual environment under joystick (desktop monitor) and physical rotation (HTC Vive head-mounted display) conditions, each preceded by a 3-minute baseline. Electrode locations were digitized with an optical tracking system.
